introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Physics 2 (0780), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2024. Time allowed: three hours.**

Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour, Section II in 30 minutes and Section III in 1 hour. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you must show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators and formulae booklet are allowed.

**Structure of the paper.** SECTION I (One hour): questions 1 to 5 are compulsory; in question 6 answer EITHER 6 (a), (b) and (c) OR 6 (d), (e) and (f). SECTION II (30 minutes): DATA ANALYSIS, question 7. SECTION III (1 hour): OPTIONS - answer any two questions from the four options (Option 1: Energy resources and environmental physics, question 8; Option 2: Communication, question 9; Option 3: Electronics, question 10; Option 4: Medical physics, question 11).

No data sheet is printed in the paper: whenever a constant is needed, the model answer states the value it uses.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Figure 10 shows a photovoltaic plate with a power output of $30\ \mathrm{mW\,cm^{-2}}$ and an efficiency of $40\%$.

![fig-1](gce-al-physics-2024-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_8_fig_1.png)

Determine

(i) the amount of solar energy falling on it per unit time;

(ii) how many such plates can supply energy directly to a 3 horse power electric pump switched on for $20$ minutes if the intensity of solar radiation is assumed constant within this time and $1\ \mathrm{hp} = 800\ \mathrm{W}$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The plate measures $1.5\ \mathrm{m}\times1.0\ \mathrm{m}$, so its area is $A = 1.5\ \mathrm{m^2} = 1.5\times10^{4}\ \mathrm{cm^2}$.

**(i) Solar energy falling on the plate per unit time.** The electrical power output of one plate is
$$P_{\mathrm{out}} = 30\ \mathrm{mW\,cm^{-2}}\times1.5\times10^{4}\ \mathrm{cm^2} = 4.5\times10^{5}\ \mathrm{mW} = 450\ \mathrm{W}.$$
Since $\text{efficiency} = \dfrac{P_{\mathrm{out}}}{P_{\mathrm{in}}}$,
$$P_{\mathrm{in}} = \frac{450}{0.40} = 1.1\times10^{3}\ \mathrm{W}\ (1125\ \mathrm{J\,s^{-1}}).$$
About $1.1\times10^{3}\ \mathrm{J}$ of solar energy falls on the plate every second (an intensity of $75\ \mathrm{mW\,cm^{-2}} = 750\ \mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$).

**(ii) Number of plates.** Power of the pump: $P = 3\times800 = 2400\ \mathrm{W}$. In $20\ \mathrm{min} = 1200\ \mathrm{s}$ the pump needs
$$E = Pt = 2400\times1200 = 2.88\times10^{6}\ \mathrm{J},$$
while one plate delivers $450\times1200 = 5.4\times10^{5}\ \mathrm{J}$ in the same time. Number of plates:
$$N = \frac{2.88\times10^{6}}{5.4\times10^{5}} = \frac{2400}{450} = 5.33.$$
A whole number of plates is needed, and $5$ plates give only $2250\ \mathrm{W} < 2400\ \mathrm{W}$, so **6 plates** are needed.

**(i) Environmentally friendly.** Producing electricity or heat from sunlight releases no carbon dioxide or other greenhouse gases, no smoke, no acid-forming gases and no radioactive or other waste during operation, so it does not pollute the air, water or soil or contribute to global warming.

**(ii) Functional.** It can be put to practical use: photovoltaic cells convert it directly to electricity (pumps, lighting, calculators, telecommunication equipment) and solar collectors convert it to heat (water heating, drying crops). It works in remote areas that have no connection to the electricity grid and needs very little maintenance.

**(iii) Renewable.** The Sun will go on radiating energy for billions of years, and the energy is continually replenished: using it does not use it up, unlike fossil fuels, which take millions of years to form.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) What is climate change?

(ii) Name two climate-change related disasters.

(iii) State two human activities that lead to climate change.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** Climate change is a long-term change (over decades or longer) in the average weather patterns of the Earth or of a region (temperature, rainfall, winds), in particular the present global warming caused by the increase of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere.

**(ii)** Any two of: floods, droughts, hurricanes and cyclones, heat waves, wildfires, sea-level rise and coastal erosion, desertification (for example the shrinking of Lake Chad).

**(iii)** Any two of: burning fossil fuels (power stations, vehicles, generators); deforestation and bush burning (less carbon dioxide absorbed); industrial processes (for example cement making); intensive agriculture (methane from livestock and rice fields, nitrous oxide from fertilisers); waste burning and rubbish dumps (methane).
